name: s04-attrsearch
title: Attribute lookup climbs the class tree
spec: A vertical chain of four boxes with upward arrows labelled not found, look next: instance (obj) at the bottom, class (Class), superclass (Base), object at the top. A side orange note: first match wins. A side grey note: no match anywhere raises AttributeError. Left code chip: obj.name.
anchor: ### Attribute search climbs a class tree
alt: Attribute lookup climbs the class tree
cap: Attribute search: Python looks in the instance, then the class, then each superclass, and the first match wins.

name: s04-assignstore
title: Where an assignment stores an attribute
spec: Two panels. Left panel code chip obj.x = 1 with arrow to a box instance obj containing x = 1 (only this object). Right panel code chip Class.x = 1 with arrow to a box Class containing x = 1 with arrows to the instances obj1 and obj2 labelled shared by every instance (orange).
anchor: ### Where an assignment stores an attribute
cap: Assignment through an instance stores on that instance, while assignment through the class is shared by all instances.

name: s04-mro
title: The method resolution order
spec: A diamond: class A at the top, classes B and C beneath it both pointing up to A, class D at the bottom pointing up to B and C, with code chip class D(B, C). Beside it an ordered list titled MRO: D, B, C, A, object with numbers 1 to 5. Orange note: super() calls the next class in this order.
cap: Inheritance: Python searches classes in the method resolution order, and super() moves to the next one.

name: s04-composition
title: Is-a versus has-a
spec: Two panels. Left panel header Inheritance (is-a): box Child with an arrow up to box Parent, note tightly coupled. Right panel header Composition (has-a, green): box Pipeline with two arrows to small boxes Client and Logger, note parts can be swapped. Bottom bar: prefer composition over inheritance.
cap: Composition: an object that has parts can swap them, while inheritance couples a child to its parent.

name: s04-abc
title: Abstract base classes
spec: Left box abstract class Provider with @abstractmethod fetch. Two boxes below pointing up with inherit arrows: class GoodProvider defines fetch (green, can be created) and class BadProvider forgets fetch (orange, TypeError when you create it). Note: the check happens at instantiation.
alt: An abstract base class enforcing a method
cap: Abstract base classes: a subclass that forgets an abstract method cannot be instantiated.

name: s04-protocol
title: Protocols match by shape
spec: Left box Protocol Reader requires read(). Right two boxes: class FileReader with read() (green, matches) and class Plain without read() (orange, does not match). No inheritance arrows from the class boxes. Comparison strip: ABC is by name (must inherit), Protocol is by shape (has the methods).
cap: A Protocol is satisfied by any class that has the right methods, with no inheritance needed.

name: s04-dataclass
title: What @dataclass writes for you
spec: Left box: a short class with @dataclass and two fields host: str and port: int. Arrow to right box of three generated methods: __init__(host, port), __repr__, __eq__. Green note: less boilerplate, the same behaviour.
cap: A dataclass generates __init__, __repr__ and __eq__ from the field list.

name: s04-typehints
title: Type hints are checked before running
spec: Left box: code with hints def start(port: int) -> bool. Two arrows. Top arrow to a green box static checker (mypy or pyright) reads the hints before the program runs and reports mismatches. Bottom arrow to an orange box at run time Python ignores the hints.
cap: Type hints are read by a static checker before running, and Python itself does not enforce them at run time.
